newsitem.title: USA: Regulators to order airbag cutoff switches -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Regulators to order airbag cutoff switches -- paper.

text.p: Federal safety regulators are set to order carmakers to make airbag cutoff switches optional on all new vehicles immediately and mandate so-called "smart" airbags, according to an article in the current issue of Automotive News.
The proposals come in the midst of a furor over airbag safety.
The switches would enable drivers to manually disconnect or engage the actuator system for the passenger-side airbag, depending on who was seated there, the newspaper said.

Citing sources close to the discussions, the newspaper said the proposal by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration also requires warning labels in vehicles and allows automakers to cut the power of driver and passenger side airbag inflators by as much as 30 percent. That would be accomplished by changing crash-test parameters, it reported.

The proposals have been sent to U.S. Transportation Secretary Frederica Pena and, if approved, will be sent to the Office of Management and Budget for a cost-benefit appraisal. Assuming an expedited review due to the urgency of the issue a binding rule could be issued this month, Automotive News said.
